back: The stage when the reproductive organs mature and the secondary sexual characteristics develop.
Penis and testes grow, sperm production begins, facial and body hair grow, the voice deepens, muscles develop.
Breasts develop, hips widen, the uterus and vagina grow and the menstrual cycle begins.

front: Main stages of a 28-day menstrual cycle
back: Days 1 to 5 menstruation; days 6 to 13 lining repairs and thickens; about day 14 ovulation; days 15 to 28 lining maintained.

front: What is **ovulation**, and when does it usually happen?
back: The release of an egg from an ovary, about 14 days before the next period (around day 14 of a 28-day cycle).

front: Role of oestrogen in the cycle
back: Repairs and thickens the lining of the uterus.

front: Role of progesterone in the cycle
back: Maintains the thick lining; when it falls, the lining breaks down.
notes: Made by the corpus luteum, and in pregnancy by the placenta.

back: Made by the pituitary gland; makes a follicle develop in the ovary and secrete oestrogen.
Made by the pituitary gland; a surge of LH triggers ovulation and the formation of the corpus luteum.

front: Why are there no periods in pregnancy?
back: Progesterone stays high (corpus luteum, then placenta), so the lining is maintained.
The few days around ovulation: sperm survive up to about five days and the egg about one day.
